body:
(same as https://github.com/Consensys/teku/pull/10457)

## PR Description

This PR optimises the deserialization of some Engine API requests. Most requests to return blobs return large hex strings as the data's byte representation, so they require some extra care on deserialization to avoid unnecessary overhead.

Summary of changes:
- Updated the deserialization logic on Bytes-related Jackson deserializers used on Engine API calls. Stopped using `getValueAsString()` to avoid allocating intermediate strings and added a more streamlined lookup table for hex to byte conversion.
- Avoiding excessive Java reflection calls with Jackson
    - By explicitly using `@JsonCreator`, and
    - By using Jackson's `Blackbird` module.

I added both JMH benchmarks used to enable easier testing for further improvements.

## Fixed Issue(s)
N/A

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches Engine API JSON deserialization (hex bytes parsing and Web3j `ObjectMapper` configuration), so regressions could break execution client communication despite added tests/benchmarks.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Improves Engine API deserialization performance** by rewriting `Bytes*` Jackson deserializers to share a new `AbstractBytesDeserializer` that parses hex directly from the parser’s char buffer (avoiding `getValueAsString()` allocations) and uses a lookup-table based hex decoder.
> 
> **Reduces Jackson reflection overhead** by adding `@JsonCreator` to key Engine API schema constructors and registering Jackson `BlackbirdModule` in `Web3jHttpClient` (plus adding the `jackson-module-blackbird` dependency).
> 
> Adds JMH benchmarks for bytes deserializers and full Engine API payload/blob response deserialization, adds unit tests covering hex parsing edge-cases, and updates an SSZ benchmark to consume results via `Blackhole` to avoid dead-code elimination.
>

author: ashleyzhang01
body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
## FEATURE: Automatically Downsize Large Images on Upload

### Summary
This change introduces automatic server-side image downsizing during upload, allowing users to upload large images that exceed the configured size limit without having their upload rejected. Instead of failing, the server will iteratively reduce the image size until it fits within the allowed limit.

### Changes

#### Client-Side Upload Validation (`utilities.js`)
- Replaced the dynamic site setting-based file size check (`max_image_size_kb`) with a hardcoded **10MB** limit for both client-side validation and the 413 (entity too large) error response. This raises the effective client-side threshold to allow large images to reach the server for processing.

#### Server-Side Auto-Downsizing (`uploads_controller.rb`)
- Increased the API image download limit to **10MB** (previously derived from `max_image_size_kb`).
- Added a downsizing loop after receiving an image upload: if the uploaded image exceeds the configured `max_image_size_kb` site setting, the server will automatically attempt to reduce the image to **80% of its current size**, repeating up to **5 times**, until the image fits within the allowed size limit. This applies only to recognized image file types.

#### Image Optimization Refactoring (`optimized_image.rb`)
- Refactored the `optimize`, `resize`, and `downsize` methods to accept a combined `dimensions` string directly, instead of separate `width` and `height` parameters. This simplifies the internal API and removes the now-redundant `dimensions` helper method.
- Added a new overloaded `downsize` method accepting a pre-formatted dimensions string (e.g., `"80%"`), enabling the percentage-based downsizing used in the upload controller.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

### Motivation

- Public profiles were able to persist and render more than the intended maximum of links, and mode (DSP) links vs social links were not separated for the left/right layout.
- The UX rules require a strict cap: max 6 total links, max 4 mode links (left), social links on the right filling remaining slots, and social links should be trimmed first when exceeding the cap.
- The API and editor flows must enforce the same rules at save/add time to prevent inconsistent state between editor and public profiles.

### Description

- Added a shared helper `apps/web/lib/profile/social-link-limits.ts` implementing the cap policy (`MAX_PROFILE_LINKS = 6`, `MAX_MODE_LINKS = 4`) and `capProfileLinkInputs` to trim API payloads.
- Enforced caps at save time by trimming incoming payloads in `PUT /api/dashboard/social-links` via `capProfileLinkInputs` so persisted links never exceed the rules.
- Split and prioritized public profile links in `useProfileShell` using `applyPublicProfileLinkCaps` so calling code receives `modeLinks` (left) and `socialLinks` (right).
- Updated `ProfileShell` to render `modeLinks` first (left) and `socialLinks` second (right) so the UI respects the new layout rules.
- Updated context-aware ordering in `lib/utils/context-aware-links.ts` to prioritize the detected source platform first (instead of hiding it), then action links, then preserve remaining order.
- Enforced the same capacity rules in the dashboard editor `useLinksManager` add flow to prevent adding beyond allowed capacity client-side.
- Tests and adjustments: added `apps/web/tests/unit/profile/social-link-limits.test.ts` and updated `useLinksManager` tests to reflect cap behavior; applied formatting and lint fixes to touched files.

author: tovarsh
body:
### Motivation
- Switching the active language could leave the preview partially rendered because Obsidian can reuse DOM nodes and previously applied inline `display:none` styles survive a rapid rerender. 
- The same transient/incomplete rendering could occur when frontmatter-driven language overrides refresh a single leaf.

### Description
- Add a lightweight debounced/stabilized second pass after language changes using a `languageRefreshToken` and `scheduleStabilizedRefresh` to re-run `refreshAllViews` after a short delay (80ms) to avoid transient partial renders.
- Introduce `resetPreviewDisplayState(view)` which clears inline `display` styles under the preview root (`.markdown-preview-view`) to remove stale `display:none` before forcing a rerender.
- Call `resetPreviewDisplayState` before invoking preview rerender in `refreshAllViews` and in the frontmatter override refresh path for consistent behavior.
- Changes applied in `main.ts` to coordinate immediate and stabilized refreshes while preserving existing cache-clearing and editor-extension dispatch logic.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run test:syntax`, all syntax tests passed (4/4). 
- Ran `npm run build` (TypeScript checks + bundling) which completed successfully.

author: izza-mus
body:
closes #133
closes #161
closes #115
 

## Summary
Introduces **public user profiles** with privacy controls, allowing users to view other users' profiles, hosted events, and send friend requests. Private profiles are only visible to friends.
### Key Features
#### Public Profiles (`/users/:id`)
- View any user's profile with bio, location, and list of hosted events
- Shows friendship status with actionable buttons (Add Friend, Cancel Request, etc.)
- Displays public information: name, bio, city, country, profile picture
- Lists all published (non-draft) events hosted by the user
#### Privacy Settings
- New `isProfilePublic` field allows users to control profile visibility
- **Private profiles** are only accessible to:
  - The user themselves
  - Their confirmed friends
- Non-friends attempting to view private profiles receive 404 responses (consistent across all endpoints to prevent user enumeration)
#### Enhanced User Data
- **New user fields**: `bio` (max 150 chars), `city`, `country`
- Input validation ensures no empty/whitespace-only values
- All fields are optional and can be updated via `PATCH /users/me`
#### Friendship Status API
- New endpoint: `GET /users/me/friends/status/:userId`
- Returns status: `none`, `pending_sent`, `pending_received`, `friends`, or `self`
- Powers the friend action buttons on public profiles

## Backend 
### Database Schema
```ts
model User {
  // New fields:
  bio             String?
  city            String?
  country         String?
  isProfilePublic Boolean @default(true)
}
```
#### New Endpoints

- GET /users/:id - Fetch public user profile (respects privacy settings)
- GET /users/:id/events - Fetch user's published events (respects privacy)
- GET /users/me/friends/status/:userId - Check friendship status between current user and target user
- 
#### Access Control
- Privacy checks enforce consistent 404 responses for private profiles
- Friend-only access validated through bidirectional friendship queries
- Security fix: Both profile and events endpoints return 404 (not 403) to prevent information disclosure
#### Validation Improvements
- Added .trim().min(1) to bio, city, and country fields
- Prevents empty/whitespace-only values from being saved


## Frontend Changes
#### New Routes
- `/users/:id` - Public profile page with profile info, friend status, and hosted events. _Did it with ids but we can change to name_

#### New reusable components:
- AnimatedUnderline - Smooth underline hover effect for navigation elements
- BackButton - Consistent back navigation (event page, edit, etc).
- EmptyState - Centralized empty state UI
- PasswordInput - Password field with show/hide toggle
- RadioCard - Card-style radio button groups
- Input with clearable prop - Shows X button to clear input

#### Navigation Improvements
- Redesigned Navbar with improved mobile menu behavior
- Mobile navigation now properly closes on route changes (fixes #161)
- Consistent container layout across all pages _again_

#### My Events Page Redesign
- Complete UI overhaul with better sorting and filtering
- Tabs for "Upcoming" and "Past" events
- Visual indicators for draft events
- Location preview with city/country
- Improved date formatting and event card design
- 
#### Style Enhancements
- more consistent spacing and typography
- Better responsive layouts
#### Technical Improvements
**Service Layer**
- userGetPublic() - Returns sanitized user data with privacy checks
- userGetPublicEvents() - Returns only published events with privacy enforcement
- Conversation service now includes event slug for easier deep linking
**Data Loaders**
- Async data fetching for profile, events, and friendship status
- Error handling with proper fallbacks
**Security Fixes**
- Information disclosure fix: Changed events endpoint from 403 to 404 for private profiles to avoid enumeration attack.
- Input validation (at least for PATCH user) prevents XSS via whitespace-only fields

## Breaking Changes
None. All changes are additive with sensible defaults:
- isProfilePublic defaults to true for existing users
- New fields are optional and backward compatible
- migration file is added

New FE E2E test coverage:
- Public profile page rendering and interactions
- Privacy enforcement for private profiles
- Friend status display and actions
- My events page with sorting and filtering

author: kamilaserpa
body:
## 🤔 Problem
Entregar ** Download e API de status** do serviço de vídeos (ROADMAP): endpoint de detalhe do vídeo (GET /videos/:id), download do ZIP de resultado (GET /videos/:id/download) somente para o dono e com status `completed`, e melhorar o roteamento com **chi** (uma rota por path em vez de dispatch manual).
## 🧐 Solution
- **Detalhe:** `GET /videos/{id}` — valida `X-User-Id`, retorna vídeo em JSON só se for do usuário; 404 se não existir ou não for dono.
- **Download:** `GET /videos/{id}/download` — valida dono e status `completed`, faz stream do ZIP do storage; 400 se ainda pending/processing/failed.
- **Service:** `GetByIDForUser(ctx, userID, videoID)` e `DownloadResultZip(ctx, userID, videoID)` em `application/service.go`; uso do mesmo `Storage` já usado no upload.
- **Chi:** substituição do `ServeMux` por `chi.Router`; rotas explícitas: `GET/POST /videos/`, `GET /videos/{id}`, `GET /videos/{id}/download`, `POST /videos/upload`, `GET /videos/health`; middleware `RequireUserIDHandler` para rotas protegidas; handlers `List`, `Create`, `GetByID`, `Download` (id via `chi.URLParam`).
- **Dockerfile:** instalação do ffmpeg para o processador de frames no worker.
- **README:** documentação dos novos endpoints e exemplos de curl; menção ao chi na arquitetura.
- **Bruno:** coleções para GetById e Download.
## 🤨 Rationale
- Chi mantém a interface stdlib (`http.Handler`, `http.ResponseWriter`), reduz código de dispatch manual e deixa uma rota por path no `main`.
- Download via stream do storage (sem redirecionar para S3) para manter o mesmo adapter de storage em dev e prod.

### Motivation

- Introduce a structured multi-course branching memory model to support independent course progress with a shared global knowledge trunk and automated code-executed state changes. 
- Provide a reproducible, code-first way to manage course-to-book-to-source mappings and safe promotion of cross-course conclusions into a global memory. 

### Description

- Add `tools/branch_memory.py` which implements `BranchMemoryManager` and `MergePolicy`, provides JSON-backed storage (`global_memory.json`, `global_candidates.json`, `merge_policy.json`, `learning_journal.json`), and exposes CLI commands `init`, `add-course-note`, `add-global-candidate`, `merge`, and `simulate-flow` to manage and test flows. 
- Implement merge logic that groups candidate global entries by `key` and promotes items only when they satisfy the configured `min_confidence`, `min_unique_courses`, and `min_occurrences` policy. 
- Add README documentation describing the multi-course branching memory design, key state files, mapping conventions, code execution management (`plan`/`apply`/`report`), conflict-resolution priorities, and maintenance guidance. 
- Include a `simulate_learning_flow` routine to demonstrate a full lifecycle from course creation through candidate promotion and course completion. 

### Testing

- Executed an end-to-end smoke simulation with `python tools/branch_memory.py simulate-flow --reset` which completed successfully and returned merged global keys as expected. 
- Ran CLI smoke commands `python tools/branch_memory.py init` and `python tools/branch_memory.py merge` to validate storage initialization and merge behavior, and both succeeded.

### Motivation
- The frontend and Apps Script sheet schemas diverged (books gained `metric/total/current`, groceries use `name/needsRefill/typicalPrice/lastPurchased`, books queue is an array of strings), causing cloud round-trips to corrupt or lose Books / Groceries / Health memory.

### Description
- Aligned sheet column definitions by updating `BOOK_COLS` and `GROCERY_COLS` to match the frontend data shape and added `LEGACY_*` column arrays for backward compatibility.
- Added `getHeaders(ss, sheetName)` and conditional readers that detect legacy vs new sheet headers and parse Books and Groceries accordingly so old spreadsheets still load safely.
- Normalized `booksQueue` to a simple string list on load/save and updated the write paths to persist `metric/total/current` for books and `needsRefill/typicalPrice/lastPurchased` for groceries.

### Motivation
- Provide a way to aggressively reduce client memory/visual cost by hiding mob parts while preserving boss parts and give operators more consolidated controls for performance and quality-of-life features.
- Improve the UI with a reusable slider widget and reorganize tabs so performance, ops, and settings are easier to find.
- Ensure any runtime changes (hidden mob parts, UI state) are cleaned up on shutdown.

### Description
- Added `ReplicatedStorage` usage and implemented mob culling features with `isBossMobPart`, `resolveMobsAssetsFolder`, `hideMobPart`, `restoreHiddenMobParts`, and `applyMobPartsCull` to hide non-boss `BasePart` descendants under `ReplicatedStorage.Assets.Mobs` and restore them when disabled.

- Added a quick-kill UI button to immediately request shutdown and updated `requestShutdown` to call `applyMobPartsCull(false)` when culling is active so hidden parts are restored on shutdown.

author: retricsu
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes synchronous file I/O blocking in FNN log handling (Issue #73).

## Problem

The original implementation used `appendFileSync` which blocks the Node.js event loop during high-volume log output. Under heavy load (e.g., active gossip sync), this could cause:
- Event loop blocking
- Pipe buffer filling up
- FNN process stalling

## Solution

Replaced synchronous file operations with asynchronous WriteStream-based implementation:

### Changes Made

1. **New LogWriter class** (`packages/cli/src/lib/log-writer.ts`)
   - Uses Node.js `WriteStream` with backpressure handling
   - 16KB buffer for efficient batching
   - Rate-limited error logging to stderr
   - Proper cleanup on flush

2. **Converted appendToTodayLog() to async** (`packages/cli/src/lib/log-files.ts`)
   - Now returns `Promise<void>`
   - Uses LogWriter with instance caching
   - Added `flushPendingLogs()` for shutdown coordination

3. **Added graceful shutdown** (`packages/cli/src/lib/node-start.ts`)
   - Calls `flushPendingLogs()` with 5-second timeout
   - Ensures pending writes complete before exit

4. **Converted runtime alert backends** (`packages/runtime/src/alerts/backends/file-jsonl.ts`)

author: chaliy
body:
## What
Add `DefaultBodyLimit::max(10 * 1024 * 1024)` (10MB) layer to the session files router.

## Why
Axum default body limit is 2MB. Base64 encoding inflates binary content ~33%, so any file over ~1.5MB gets rejected with HTTP 413. This blocks legitimate file uploads via the session filesystem API.

## How
Added `DefaultBodyLimit` import and `.layer(DefaultBodyLimit::max(10 * 1024 * 1024))` to the `routes()` function in `session_files.rs`, matching the existing pattern in `images.rs` and `skills.rs`.

## Risk
- Low
- Only affects max request body size for session file routes. No behavioral change for requests under 2MB.

- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Backward compatibility considered

author: caioferreirab
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive backend for managing "Entrevista por Competências" (Competency Interview) for adult volunteers in the scouting system. It adds a new API for interview management, integrates with a large language model (LLM) to generate interview summaries, and updates portal access to include new routes and permissions for adult management features.

Key changes include:

**1. API for Gestão de Adultos (Adult Management):**
- Introduces a new module `gris/api/gestao_adultos/endpoints.py` that provides endpoints for listing, retrieving, creating, and saving interviews, as well as managing interview forms and options. It includes robust access control and data serialization logic.
- Exports these endpoints in the `gris/api/gestao_adultos/__init__.py` for use elsewhere in the application.

**2. LLM Integration for Interview Summaries:**
- Implements an LLM client in `gris/api/llm/client.py` to interact with OpenRouter (OpenAI-compatible) for generating text completions, with error handling and configuration via Frappe doctype.
- Adds a summary service (`summary_service.py`) that builds the interview context and uses the LLM client to generate a professional, structured summary of the interview.
- Provides background task management (`summary_tasks.py`) for enqueuing and processing interview summary generation, updating the interview document with the generated summary.
- Includes a prompt builder (`prompt_builder.py`) that defines the system prompt and user prompt construction for consistent LLM output.
- Adds error classes for LLM configuration and request failures.
- Exports the main LLM client function in `gris/api/llm/__init__.py`.

**3. Portal Access and Permissions:**
- Updates `portal_access.py` to add new navigation entries for "Gestão de Adultos," including routes for interviews and personal interview access.
- Configures access control for the new pages, ensuring only users with the "Gestor de Adultos" role (or all users for personal interview) can access the relevant routes.
- Adds a helper function to check if a user has a personal interview record.

These changes collectively enable robust management of adult competency interviews, including secure access, data handling, and automated, LLM-powered interview summaries.

author: arimendelow
body:
## What shipped
- BlueBubbles now keeps one persisted session trunk per chat instead of splitting every reply thread into its own long-lived `_thread_*.json` memory lane.
- Thread information is still preserved, but only as current-turn metadata injected into the inbound turn, so Slugger can narrow correctly for a threaded reply without forgetting the parent conversation.
- BlueBubbles now removes obsolete sibling `_thread_*.json` session artifacts for a live chat trunk before loading the session, which prevents old broken thread lanes from re-poisoning the conversation.
- The reply-targeting send path remains intact; threaded sends still use the existing `replyToMessageGuid` behavior.
- Tests now cover DM and group routing, top-level vs threaded scope metadata, narrow cleanup behavior, and cleanup failure logging, and the release is versioned as `0.1.0-alpha.30`.

## Why this matters
- iMessage reply threads should feel like focused branches inside one ongoing conversation, not like brand-new people or blank-slate chats.
- This closes the AX failure where Slugger could suddenly re-open with messages like `hiya, what do ya need help with?` in the middle of active work just because the human replied in-thread.
- The cleanup path makes the fix durable on real machines that already accumulated broken per-thread session artifacts.
- The implementation stays intentionally simple: one chat trunk, per-turn scope metadata, and preserved reply targeting, instead of a heavier multi-lane persistence model.

## How to try it yourself
1. From a clean shell, update and restart the runtime:
   - `cd ~`
   - `npx ouro.bot up`
   - `ouro -v`
2. Confirm the new runtime is active:
   - `ouro status`
   - verify the reported version is `0.1.0-alpha.30`
3. In iMessage with Slugger, send a normal top-level task message, then reply to one of Slugger's messages in-thread, then switch back to a top-level follow-up.
4. Inspect the persisted session directory if you want to prove the file-level behavior:
   - `ls ~/.agentstate/slugger/sessions/<friend-id>/bluebubbles`
   - you should see the main chat trunk file, and no new `*_thread_*.json` session files for that chat.

## Verification
- `npm test`
  - passed: `137` test files, `2569` tests passed, `18` skipped
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
  - passed
- `npm run test:coverage`
  - passed with `100%` statements / branches / functions / lines and `nerves audit: pass`
- Targeted artifacts are recorded in:
  - `/Users/arimendelow/AgentBundles/ouroboros.ouro/tasks/one-shots/2026-03-09-1742-doing-bluebubbles-cross-thread-awareness/`

## Live agent validation
- This task was grounded in a real Slugger/Ari iMessage failure where one DM accumulated multiple `_thread_*.json` BlueBubbles session files and produced mid-task resets.
- The live Ari/Slugger session state was manually cleaned back to the main trunk before implementation, and the shipped cleanup helper now automates removal of those obsolete thread-lane files for future turns.
- No separate post-fix iMessage chat transcript was captured in this PR; live validation here is the real-session diagnosis plus the persisted-session cleanup behavior, backed by the targeted and full automated test suites.

author: bohutang
body:
Closes #115

## Summary

This PR fixes five confirmed P0 issues identified through static analysis of the codebase.

## Changes

### 1. Missing `unhandledRejection` handler (`index.ts`)
Without this handler, unhandled promise rejections silently crash the Electron main process in Node.js 15+. Added a handler that logs the rejection reason.

### 2. SQLite missing `foreign_keys` and `journal_mode` pragmas (`database.ts`)
SQLite disables foreign key enforcement by default, allowing orphaned records and referential integrity violations. WAL mode also improves concurrent read performance and crash safety. Both pragmas are now set in the constructor.

### 3. Removed broken `transactionAsync` (`database.ts`)
The method wrapped an async function inside a `better-sqlite3` synchronous transaction callback. Since `better-sqlite3` transactions are synchronous, the transaction committed before the async work completed — making the transaction semantics completely ineffective. The method was unused, so it was removed.

### 4. Mutex race condition fix (`mutex.ts`)
The previous implementation used a polling loop (`setTimeout(10ms)`) to wait for lock release. This has a TOCTOU race: two concurrent callers could both observe the lock as free between the `while` check and the `locks.set` call. Replaced with a proper queue-based implementation using promise callbacks — no polling, no race condition, and waiters are notified immediately on release.

### 5. PID validation before shell interpolation (`SessionManager.ts`, `AbstractExecutor.ts`)
`parentPid` and `pid` values were interpolated directly into shell command strings (`wmic`, `ps`, `taskkill`) without validation. A non-integer value could inject arbitrary shell commands. Added integer validation (`Math.floor` + `Number.isInteger` + `> 0`) before any shell interpolation.

### Motivation
- Improve the HomeFit IA exercise experience by providing richer guidance (video + textual), voice instructions, background music support and a basic exercise prescription/profile to better tailor goals and safety guidance.
- Standardize per-exercise durations to longer, safer blocks and require users to view an embedded tutorial before starting real execution to reduce injury risk.

### Description
- HTML: removed the old `ex-setup-panel`, updated the `hf-duration` slider range and default, changed timer display text, added `hf-music-bg` iframe block and an in-app `hf-prescription` information panel, and relabeled music control to indicate background playback.
- Data/profile: added `calorieNeed` to `userDataCache` and introduced `getExercisePrescriptionProfile()` to infer age, intensity factors, protocol and a daily goal based on IMC and stored data.
- Exercise generation: added a local `VIDEO_DB` catalog, `toEmbed()` helper, `generateLocal()` fallback generator and `askExerciseAI()` that attempts a proxy AI call and falls back to local content; `hf-generate` now uses the AI proxy with offline fallback.
- UI/UX and timers: changed `homeFitState` defaults to 60s exercise blocks, added `tutorialDone` gating, added `speakSequence()` for queued speech, updated `autoTime()` logic, require watching the tutorial video and clicking `Fim de tutorial` before `start` is allowed, and improved timer start/pause behavior to cancel speech synthesis when paused.
- Safety and guidance: `renderExerciseProgress()` now injects a prescription summary into `hf-prescription` using the computed profile, and `markComplete()` shows a rest note in the completion alert.
- Background music: `hf-open-music` now reveals the embedded YouTube iframe and starts background playback instead of opening a new window.

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce memory use for long WAV files and add robust chunked processing and CSV export for DIFAR bearing time series.
- Improve ±180° ambiguity resolution feedback from OMNI-derived active-intensity and only apply continuity fallback when needed.
- Add target profile management and metadata (profile id / classification) to DIFAR processing and persistence for better analysis workflows.
- Extend the DIFAR simulator to support multi-target schedules and better sync with host app context, and improve chart/GUI integration for DIFAR overlays.

### Description
- Refactored `compute_bearing_time_series` and `_resolve_180_by_omni_active_intensity` to return a `(bearing_deg, used_intensity)` pair and only apply continuity disambiguation when OMNI-based disambiguation was not used.
- Extracted CSV output logic into `_write_bearing_timeseries_csv` and added `process_wav_to_bearing_time_series_chunked` which reads WAV files in chunks, merges chunk outputs, and optionally writes CSVs to limit memory use for long files.
- Enhanced tools and UI: added a DIFAR event list to the chart sidebar, selection filtering for DIFAR overlays, and a refresh helper `_refresh_difar_event_list` in `main_app_refactored.py`.
- Extended `tools_difar.py` with compatibility helpers, DB migrations and new columns (`target_profile_id`, `target_classification`), a `difar_target_profiles` table with seed profiles, target-profile UI and management, bandpass/band looping for multi-band runs, optional chunked processing checkbox and parameters, and improved saving of results and map rays (including storing profile metadata and run tags).
- Updated simulator (`tools_difar_simulator.py`) to support multi-target schedules via a parsed CSV-like text area, per-target synthesis aggregation, added `_sync_context_from_host` to inherit `project_id` and output directory from host window, and replaced CSV parsing with `csv.DictReader` and batched DB inserts for track points.

### Testing
- Ran the project test suite with `pytest -q` and the tests completed successfully with no regressions observed.
- Performed automated smoke runs invoking `process_wav_to_bearing_time_series_chunked` on short WAV samples to verify chunk merging and CSV export behavior and they succeeded.

body: **What is this feature?** This feature introduces a new user preference called "Compact Mode" that allows users to switch between the default and a more compact navigation layout. **Why do we need this feature?** Users often prefer to customize their UI density to maximize screen real estate. This preference provides an option to reduce the visual footprint of the main navigation, offering a more streamlined experience for those who prefer it. **Who is this feature for?** This feature is for all Grafana users who wish to customize their user interface, particularly those who prefer a more compact navigation menu to gain more space for dashboards and other content. **Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**: Fixes # **Special notes for your reviewer:** Please check that: - [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective. - The `Compact mode` toggle is available in the user profile settings. - Toggling it on/off and saving correctly updates the user's preference. - The navigation layout (mega menu docked/undocked state) changes immediately and persists across page refreshes and sessions. - [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle. (N/A, this is a user preference) - [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc. **Implementation details:** * **Backend:** `compactMode` field added to `pkg/api/dtos/prefs.go`, preference service models, and API endpoints (Update/Patch/Get). Legacy preference registry mapping is also updated. * **Frontend:** A "Compact mode" switch is added to `UserProfileEditForm.tsx`. The profile update payload is extended to include this preference, which is then patched to `/api/user/preferences`. * **Layout Wiring:** The app chrome reads this preference to control the mega menu's docked/undocked behavior. Local storage is also synced on profile save for consistent post-refresh behavior. * **Tests:** Targeted Go tests for preference service and API, and frontend tests for the profile form and MegaMenu behavior have been updated/added. A walkthrough video demonstrating the functionality is available in the final commit message. ---

> ### 3) Output-path support
> Support:
> - output to a directory for batch generation
> - output to a specific PDF path only when a single input file is being processed
> 
> Mirror the current CV behavior where sensible.
> 
> ### 4) Cache-aware skip behavior
> Use hash-based caching so unchanged cover-letter inputs are skipped.
> 
> However, do **not** key only on the JSON file. The cache invalidation strategy must account for all relevant inputs, including at least:
> - the cover-letter JSON file
> - the selected layout template(s)
> - any shared cover-letter partial templates used to build the output
> - optionally the generator version or a cache schema version
> 
> ### 5) Duplicate avoidance
> Do not regenerate outputs when there are no meaningful changes.
> 
> This issue should explicitly ensure that duplicate work is avoided for cover letters the same way the project already avoids unnecessary CV regeneration.
> 
> ### 6) Verbose mode
> Support a verbose mode similar to the existing script so users can see:
> - which files were discovered
> - which files were skipped due to cache
> - which files were rendered
> - which layout was selected
> - where output PDFs were written
> 
> ### 7) Naming convention
> Implement a consistent output naming rule.
> 
> It should support:
> - default generated names from the JSON filename and language
> - optional explicit output name from the cover-letter JSON schema
> - collision-safe behavior
> 
> ### 8) Error handling
> Provide clear failures for cases like:
> - invalid JSON
> - missing required keys
> - bad template name
> - output-path misuse
> - XeLaTeX failure
> 
> ## Deliverables
> - Working CLI entry point for cover-letter generation
> - Cache-aware build behavior
> - Duplicate avoidance implemented correctly
> - Batch and single-file workflows working end-to-end
> 
> ## Acceptance criteria
> - Cover letters can be generated from the dedicated input folder.
> - Single-file and batch mode both work.

the 1.93.1 pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`

start clean and the cached artifacts are never reused.

author: krooney144
body:
Move all Overpass fetching, JSON parsing, multipolygon stitching, and river stitching off the main thread into a dedicated waterWorker.

Architecture:
- World divided into 1° × 1° tile grid
- Each tile is an independent Overpass query + IndexedDB cache entry
- Panning reuses cached tiles — only new tiles trigger network requests
- Worker runs max 2 concurrent Overpass requests to avoid rate limiting
- In-memory + IndexedDB (24h TTL) two-tier cache per tile
- Stale-while-revalidate: cached tiles render instantly, new tiles stream in as the worker completes them

Simplified Overpass query — unified water filter:
  way/relation["natural"="water"|"water"]["name"] + way["waterway"]["name"] No longer distinguishes between river/stream/lake/reservoir at query level — classification happens in post-processing.

MapScreen changes:
- Computes viewport bounds (with 25% padding for prefetch)
- Sends tile requests to worker via WaterTileManager
- Tiles arrive individually — map updates progressively
- Debug panel shows: tile count, cached/fetched/pending, Overpass timing, generation counter

Legacy fetchWaterNear() API preserved for SCAN/EXPLORE.

author: rocketman-code
body:
## Summary

Three independent fixes that eliminate architectural bug classes:

- **Replace prettyplease with ToTokens** — `prettyplease::unparse` destroys `#[cfg]` attributes on block expressions inside match arms, causing E0658 and E0433 compilation failures on projects like topgrade. syn's `ToTokens` preserves all attributes correctly. The instrumented source is compiled and discarded, so formatting quality is irrelevant.
- **TLS try_with in drop_cold** — `drop_cold` used `.with()` for RECORDS_BUF, FRAME_BUFFER, and INVOCATIONS, which panics if TLS is destroyed during thread teardown. `drain_inflight_stack` already recovers guard data via `try_with` during TlsFlushGuard drop, so skipping here is safe.
- **Whole-body PianoFuture wrapping for impl Future** — Previously only the trailing expression was wrapped, silently missing early returns. Now the entire function body is wrapped in `PianoFuture::new(async move { ... })` with an `AsyncReturnAwaiter` visitor that adds `.await` to unwrap nested `return async { ... }` expressions.

- [x] All integration tests pass
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] Piano successfully profiles topgrade (619 functions, 41 files) — previously failed with 8 E0658 + 1 E0433 errors
- [ ] Verify cfg preservation with `instrument_macros=true` on additional real-world projects
- [ ] Verify impl Future wrapping doesn't break async integration tests

Fixes #429, #511, #560, #561.

Six critical bugs and three missing features identified in a deep code review. This PR addresses the highest-priority items: two data-layer correctness bugs, a missing core trading feature, a multi-connection race condition, an unimplemented API contract, and a missing async/sync bridge primitive.

## Database (`bot/database.py`)
- **Thread-local connection pooling** via `_local = threading.local()` — replaces open-on-every-call pattern
- `_db_initialized` + `_last_initialized_path` guard: `init_db()` DDL runs once per process per path; path change (e.g. test isolation) auto-reinitializes
- `close_all_connections()` for clean shutdown; stale connection auto-detected when `_DB_PATH` changes between calls
- `_get_conn()` no longer closes the connection on exit — wraps pooled conn in a savepoint instead

## RiskManager (`bot/risk_manager.py`)
- **Dirty tracking**: `_dirty_ids: set[str]` — `_save()` only writes mutated signals and clears the set; previously wrote all signals on every price tick
- **Real trailing stop-loss**: new `TrailingStopConfig` dataclass; `ActiveSignal` gains `trailing_sl_price`, `highest_since_entry`, `lowest_since_entry`; `_update_trailing_sl()` manages LONG/SHORT high/low-water marks and closes signals on breach with reason `"trailing_sl"`; `update_prices()` accepts optional `atrs: dict[str, float]` for ATR-based trail distance

```python
# TrailingStopConfig controls behavior
cfg = TrailingStopConfig(enabled=True, atr_multiplier=1.5, activation_after_be=True, trail_step_pct=0.1)
rm = RiskManager(trailing_config=cfg)
```

## WebSocket (`bot/ws_manager.py`)
- **Per-connection health dict** `_connection_health: dict[int, float]` (conn_idx → monotonic timestamp) replaces the single shared `is_connected` bool that any connection could overwrite
- `is_healthy()` returns `True` if any connection is within `_STALE_THRESHOLD`; falls back to legacy `last_message_at`/`is_connected` when dict is empty for backward compatibility

## Exchange (`bot/exchange.py`)
- **Request weight tracking** finally implemented (was documented but absent): `_check_weight(cost)` maintains a 60-second rolling `_weight_used` counter; sleeps *outside* the lock when approaching `_WEIGHT_LIMIT - _WEIGHT_BUFFER (1100)`; lazy attribute init preserves `__new__`-based test compatibility

- `put_nowait()` for scheduler/scanner threads; `put()` async coroutine; `consume(bot)` long-running task with 50 ms rate-limit delay and per-message error isolation

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


# Comprehensive Architecture Overhaul — 360 Crypto Eye Scalping

## Overview
This PR must address **all** critical issues, architectural changes, and missing features identified in a deep line-by-line code review. The goal is to transform this project into the best all-rounder crypto signal provider on Telegram.

---

## CRITICAL ISSUES TO FIX

### 1. Split `bot/bot.py` God File (~2800+ lines, 111KB)
The single largest technical debt. `bot/bot.py` contains command handlers, scanner logic, fallback polling, spot scanning, WebSocket callbacks, scheduler jobs, channel routing, signal broadcasting, and the main loop — all in ONE file.

**Required decomposition:**
- `bot/commands/start.py` — `/start`, `/help` command handlers
- `bot/commands/scan.py` — `/scan`, `/force_scan` command handlers
- `bot/commands/risk.py` — `/risk_calc`, `/set_balance` command handlers
- `bot/commands/signals.py` — `/active`, `/close`, `/close_all` command handlers
- `bot/commands/settings.py` — `/trail_sl`, `/session_filter`, `/set_leverage` command handlers
- `bot/commands/dashboard.py` — `/dashboard`, `/performance`, `/stats` command handlers
- `bot/commands/admin.py` — `/admin`, `/broadcast`, `/status` command handlers
- `bot/commands/__init__.py` — register all command handlers
- `bot/scanners/futures_scanner.py` — extracted from `_run_fallback_scan_job()` and WebSocket candle-close callback
- `bot/scanners/spot_scanner.py` — extracted from `_run_spot_scan_job()`
- `bot/broadcast.py` — all `_broadcast*` functions, `_send_telegram_message()`, `BroadcastQueue` class
- `bot/scheduler.py` — APScheduler job registration and configuration
- `bot/app.py` — `build_application()` and `main()` entry point

Each extracted module must maintain the same functionality. All imports must be updated. The original `bot/bot.py` should become a thin orchestration layer that imports from the new modules.

### 2. Deduplicate Signal Engine Channel Functions
In `bot/signal_engine.py`, the functions `run_confluence_check`, `run_confluence_check_ch2_medium`, and `run_confluence_check_ch3_easy` share ~80% identical code (scoring blocks, gate checks, TP/SL calculations).

**Fix:**
- Create a `ChannelProfile` dataclass:
```python
@dataclass
class ChannelProfile:
    name: str
    min_confluence: int
    leverage_min: int
    leverage_max: int
    tp_ratios: tuple[float, float, float]  # (tp1_mult, tp2_mult, tp3_mult)
    require_fvg: bool = True
    require_ob: bool = True
    require_sweep: bool = True
    sl_buffer_atr_mult: float = 1.0
```
- Create predefined profiles: `CH1_HARD`, `CH2_MEDIUM`, `CH3_EASY`, `CH4_SPOT`
- Extract a single `_score_confluence(gates_passed: dict, profile: ChannelProfile) -> int` helper
- Replace the 3 duplicated functions with a single `run_confluence_check(profile: ChannelProfile, ...)` that dispatches based on profile settings
- Keep backward compatibility by having the old function names call the new unified function

### 3. Fix SQLite Connection Pooling in `bot/database.py`
Current `_get_conn()` creates a NEW connection on every call, which is inefficient and causes:
- `init_db()` being called on every `_save()` (line 102 of risk_manager.py)
- No connection reuse

**Fix:**
- Implement thread-local connection pooling:
```python
import threading
_local = threading.local()

def _get_conn_pooled() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    if not hasattr(_local, 'conn') or _local.conn is None:
        _local.conn = sqlite3.connect(_DB_PATH, check_same_thread=False)
        _local.conn.execute

author: jgop-l
body:
---                                                                                                 
  AgentScope-Java Version
                                                                                                      
  1.0.10-SNAPSHOT                                           

  Description

  Background

  When MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools return JSON Schema with $ref references, the referenced type
   definitions are stored in $defs (JSON Schema 2020-12) or definitions (legacy JSON Schema) fields.
  These definitions are essential for resolving $ref references.

  Problem

  The McpTool.convertMcpSchemaToParameters() method was only copying type, properties, required, and
  additionalProperties fields from the MCP JsonSchema. The $defs and definitions fields were being
  dropped during conversion, causing $ref references to become invalid.

  Solution

  Added logic to preserve $defs and definitions fields when converting MCP schema to AgentScope
  parameters:

  // Preserve $defs and definitions for $ref resolution
  if (inputSchema.defs() != null && !inputSchema.defs().isEmpty()) {
      parameters.put("$defs", new HashMap<>(inputSchema.defs()));
  }

  if (inputSchema.definitions() != null && !inputSchema.definitions().isEmpty()) {
      parameters.put("definitions", new HashMap<>(inputSchema.definitions()));
  }

  Changes

  - McpTool.java: Added handling for $defs and definitions fields in convertMcpSchemaToParameters()
  - McpToolTest.java: Added 3 test cases:
    - testConvertMcpSchemaToParameters_WithDefs: Tests $defs preservation
    - testConvertMcpSchemaToParameters_WithDefinitions: Tests definitions preservation
    - testConvertMcpSchemaToParameters_WithBothDefsAndDefinitions: Tests both fields together

  How to Test

  mvn test -pl agentscope-core -Dtest=McpToolTest

  Fixes #893

  - All tests are passing (mvn test)

  - Related documentation has been updated (e.g. links, examples, etc.)

author: rysweet
body:
## Summary

Implements full bidirectional hook callback protocol so the Claude Agent SDK can register and execute Python/TypeScript hook callbacks during RustyClawd's tool loop.

## Architecture

- `SdkTransport` sends `control_request` (hook_callback) to SDK via stdout
- Reads `control_response` from SDK via stdin
- `read_stream_json_stdin` now uses `read_line()` loop (not `lines()` iterator) to keep stdin open
- `tool_executor` dispatches SDK hook callbacks alongside file-based hooks

## Protocol

1. Tool fires -> check SdkHookConfig for matching callbacks
2. Send: `{"type":"control_request","request_id":"hook_req_1","request":{"subtype":"hook_callback","callback_id":"hook_0","input":{...}}}`
3. SDK runs Python callback, responds: `{"type":"control_response","response":{"request_id":"hook_req_1","output":{...}}}`
4. PreToolUse: can deny with `"decision":"deny"`. PostToolUse: fire-and-forget.

## Review findings addressed

- Blocking read_line: documented as known limitation, SDK disconnection returns broken pipe
- tool_orchestrator: SDK hooks intentionally skipped (documented)
- Fail-open policy: documented, warn logged

## Test plan

- [x] 7 sdk_transport unit tests (roundtrip, deny, empty, invalid, format, IDs)
- [x] 6 config matching tests (exact, wildcard, no match, wrong event, multiple)
- [x] Existing tests pass (tool_executor_tests updated)
- [ ] CI passes

Closes #574

This pull request introduces several improvements and refactorings to the backend chat and LLM client services, focusing on configurability, streaming robustness, and code clarity. The most significant changes include making the AI model and endpoint configurable via environment variables, improving the streaming interface between synchronous and asynchronous code, and enhancing code documentation and test coverage.

**Configurability and Environment Variables:**
- The AI model, endpoint, and token are now configurable via environment variables (`AI_MODEL`, `AI_ENDPOINT`, `AI_TOKEN`), replacing hardcoded values and previous usage of `GITHUB_TOKEN`. This allows for more flexible deployment and testing. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8448f3bb238b93cd9001fe2b84c3ee9dc89e1c3270fc7f22f525e2f23a3d90cdR19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8448f3bb238b93cd9001fe2b84c3ee9dc89e1c3270fc7f22f525e2f23a3d90cdL244-R263) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1a93b1f3a8a11a4cb2424ada98a1d59bffe817cb3854f8703bc30af01dfdae9fL17-R20) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-a6116cfd5c55f263ca6cfec133939ec093bb78db0543a7c17f7788aa5184ef95L71-R73) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-6c536d091e89248a4bc4b4f1c8c9caadc5b815cf3e3ee5958f8b94bc61041b39R22-R23) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-f46f920359af457aa5cce3b0f3434184db4eef61c002c6e6ea4721c1ecb0ff8fR3-R9) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba8abce566d15c6c78894ef7fd1bad4c4ccf86664576abc44eb854ab57426c1R37-R38) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-0ba8abce566d15c6c78894ef7fd1bad4c4ccf86664576abc44eb854ab57426c1L130-R133)

author: dobbry-vechur
body:
#### Summary
Bugfixes "Prevent pseudo-dormant monsters from upgrading before going dormant"

#### Purpose of change

Was investigating a flaky CI failure in `dormant_monsters_materialize_correctly`:
https://github.com/CleverRaven/Cataclysm-DDA/actions/runs/22867725314/job/66338936835

Didn't find the root cause of that particular failure, but noticed a latent bug: pseudo-dormant monsters inherit the `upgrades` field from their base zombie type. In a real game, `on_load()` calls `try_upgrade()` which can change the monster's type before it fires its dormant trap setup attack. If a `pseudo_dormant_mon_zombie_fat` upgrades into, say, `mon_zombie_brute`, it loses its `pseudo_dormant_trap_setup` special attack entirely and just walks around as a regular brute - the dormant corpse mechanic silently breaks for that spawn.

Doesn't manifest in tests because calendar starts at `turn_zero` so upgrades never trigger. But in a real game with actual calendar progression, a monster with `half_life: 128` has a reasonable chance of upgrading on materialization.

#### Describe the solution

Set `upgrades = false` on the generated pseudo-dormant mtype, same pattern as the generator already uses for dodge, regen, armor, etc.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered

Could set it in JSON per-monster, but since the generator already programmatically strips a bunch of stuff, this fits right in.

#### Testing

Code inspection. The generator already handles similar fields the same way.

#### Additional context

None

### Bug 1 - App stays blocked after limit increase
Root cause: ReloadConfig only swapped _config; the in-memory DailyLog retained Blocked = true entries.

Fix: ReloadConfig now iterates blocked entries and unblocks any entry whose usage is below the new per-app limit, resets WarningSent when usage is well below the new limit, clears OverallCapHit when the new overall cap exceeds current total usage or is removed, and persists every change to the DB.

### Bug 2 - No validation: break interval vs. daily limit
Fix: RuleEditWindow.OnSave rejects saves where breakEvery >= dailyLimit (both non-zero) with "Break interval must be less than the daily limit."

### Bug 3 - No validation: break duration vs. break interval
Fix: RuleEditWindow.OnSave rejects saves where breakDuration > breakEvery with "Break duration must be less than or equal to the break interval."

## Tests added / updated

| File | New tests |
|---|---|
| RulesEngineTests.cs | NoBlock_WhenEntryAlreadyBlocked, BreakDue_WhenTimeSinceBreakExceedsInterval, NoBreakDue_WhenTimeSinceBreakBelowInterval |
| MonitorServiceTests.cs (new) | 5 tests for ReloadConfig unblock behaviour (per-app + overall cap) |
| RuleEditWindowTests.cs (new) | 5 UI tests for the two new validation rules, including edge cases |

RuleEditWindow.xaml also gains AutomationProperties.AutomationId on all TextBox fields so the UI tests can locate them reliably.

author: copilot
body:
Bar load conditions (`in_combat`, `mounted`, `alive`, `in_group`, etc.) were only evaluated inside `RebuildAllBars()`, which only runs on a handful of lifecycle events (world entry, talent/spell changes). Conditions were never re-checked during normal gameplay, so e.g. entering combat wouldn't show/hide a bar with an `in_combat` condition.

- **BarManager.lua**: Added `RecheckBarConditions()` — iterates all DB bars, compares `ShouldShowBar()` against current visibility, and calls `RebuildBar()` only for bars whose state actually changed. Near-zero cost in the steady state.
- **UpdateEngine.lua**: Calls `RecheckBarConditions()` in the existing 100ms update tick, before cooldown/text updates.

```lua
function AuraTracker:RecheckBarConditions()
    local db = self:GetDB()
    if not db or not db.enabled then return end

    for barKey in pairs(db.bars) do
        local shouldShow = self:ShouldShowBar(barKey)
        local isShown    = self.bars[barKey] ~= nil

        if shouldShow ~= isShown then
            self:RebuildBar(barKey)
        end
    end
end
```

body:
Implement unit tests for `createPcmBlob` in `utils/audio-utils.ts` to ensure its reliability and coverage.

The new test file `utils/audio-utils.test.ts` covers:
- **Standard Values:** Verifies that typical audio samples (0, 0.5, -0.5, 1.0, -1.0) are correctly converted to 16-bit PCM values, including proper truncation.
- **Clamping/Clipping:** Ensures that values outside the [-1, 1] range are correctly capped at the maximum/minimum 16-bit integers.
- **Empty Input:** Checks that an empty `Float32Array` results in an empty output.
- **MIME Type:** Validates that the returned object contains the correct `audio/pcm;rate=16000` string.

Tests are implemented using the native Node.js `assert` module and can be executed with `node --experimental-strip-types utils/audio-utils.test.ts`. This approach was chosen due to network issues preventing the installation of external testing frameworks like Vitest.

author: melvincarvalho
body:
## Summary

- Adds remoteStorage protocol (draft-dejong-remotestorage-22) to JSS
- 234 lines, no new dependencies — reuses existing filesystem storage, OAuth (#161), and WebFinger
- Always on — no flag needed. Storage routes are just a path translation over existing infrastructure.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/storage/:user/*` | Read file or folder listing |
| HEAD | `/storage/:user/*` | Metadata only |
| PUT | `/storage/:user/*` | Write file |
| DELETE | `/storage/:user/*` | Delete file |

## Features

- **Directory listings** in RS JSON-LD format (`http://remotestorage.io/spec/folder-description`)
- **Public folder** (`/storage/:user/public/*`) readable without auth
- **Conditional requests** — ETags, If-Match, If-None-Match, 304 Not Modified
- **WebFinger discovery** — RS link relation added to existing WebFinger response
- **Bearer token auth** via OAuth flow from #161
- **WAC bypass** — RS routes handle their own auth (Bearer tokens, not WAC)

## How it works

```
RS path:     /storage/me/photos/vacation.jpg
             ↓ strip /storage/me
Storage:     /photos/vacation.jpg
             ↓ urlToPath()
Filesystem:  ./data/photos/vacation.jpg
```

Same files, same filesystem, same ETags. A remoteStorage.js client and a Solid client can read/write the same data.

## WebFinger

```json
{
  "rel": "http://tools.ietf.org/id/draft-dejong-remotestorage",
  "href": "https://example.com/storage/me",
  "properties": {
    "http://remotestorage.io/spec/version": "draft-dejong-remotestorage-22",
    "http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-4.2": "https://example.com/oauth/authorize",
    "http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750#section-2.3": "Bearer"
  }
}
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `GET /.well-known/webfinger?resource=acct:me@example.com` includes RS link
- [ ] `GET /storage/me/` returns folder listing in RS JSON-LD format
- [ ] `PUT /storage/me/test/hello.txt` creates file
- [ ] `GET /storage/me/test/hello.txt` returns file with ETag
- [ ] `GET /storage/me/test/hello.txt` with `If-None-Match` returns 304
- [ ] `DELETE /storage/me/test/hello.txt` with `If-Match` deletes file
- [ ] `GET /storage/me/public/` works without auth
- [ ] `PUT /storage/me/test.txt` without auth returns 401
- [ ] remoteStorage.js client can connect via WebFinger discovery

Refs #106

body:
## Summary

- Adds `genesis-auth` crate implementing OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant for OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT subscription-based inference)
- Wires OAuth credentials into `client_from_config` with automatic token refresh, in-process caching (60s TTL, double-check locking), and JWT expiry detection
- Adds `genesis login` / `genesis logout` CLI commands and integrates OAuth as an option in `genesis init` wizard
- Enhances `genesis doctor` to show OAuth credential status and token expiry info

### New crate: `genesis-auth`
- **Device code flow**: `request_device_code` → `poll_for_authorization` → `exchange_code_for_tokens` with browser auto-open
- **Token refresh**: Automatic refresh when JWT `exp` is within 120s of expiry, with 15s timeout
- **Credential caching**: Per-path `HashMap<PathBuf, CachedEntry>` behind `OnceLock<RwLock<...>>` with double-check locking to prevent thundering herd
- **Auth store**: JSON file at platform data dir with `0600` permissions, type-safe `CredentialSource` and `AuthMode` enums with kebab-case serde
- **Codex CLI migration**: Import tokens from `~/.codex/auth.json` (independent session, won't affect Codex CLI)
- **JWT utilities**: Allocation-friendly claims decoding without signature verification, used only for expiry checks
- **Provider registry**: Extensible `AuthProviderConfig` with OpenAI Codex as first provider

### Integration points
- `client_from_config` (now `async`) tries OAuth first for `openai-codex` backend, falls back to env vars
- Per-turn client rebuild in `build_agent_loop` naturally picks up refreshed tokens
- `resolve.rs` maps `openai-codex` backend to Codex inference URL

### Motivation

author: copilot
body:
Adds machine-to-machine authentication to `apps/auth-api` via the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow (RFC 6749 §4.4), enabling other APIs to authenticate without human interaction.

## New endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/oauth/clients` | Register a client app — returns a one-time `client_secret` |
| `POST` | `/oauth/token` | Exchange credentials for a ****** |

```http
POST /oauth/token
{ "grant_type": "client_credentials", "client_id": "<uuid>", "client_secret": "<secret>" }

→ 200 { "access_token": "<RS256 JWT>", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600 }
```

## Changes

- **DB** — new `oauth_clients` table (Drizzle schema + migration `0001_oauth_clients.sql`); `client_secret` stored as SHA-256 hash, plaintext returned once at registration
- **Service** — `ClientCredentialsService` validates credentials, signs an RS256 access token (reuses existing `JwtService`) with `grant_type: "client_credentials"` in payload; `expires_in` derived from JWT `exp`/`iat` claims
- **Controller** — `OAuthController` with `token` and `registerClient` handlers, following existing controller conventions
- **Validation** — Zod validators for both endpoints
- **Drizzle config** — corrected schema path (`src/database/schema.ts` → `src/schemas/database/index.ts`)

## Security note
Client secrets are hashed before storage. The `grant_type` claim in the JWT payload distinguishes machine tokens from user-issued tokens. Neither the new endpoints nor the existing `/auth/*` routes have rate limiting — `@fastify/rate-limit` is worth adding before production exposure.

author: chaliy
body:
## What
When the Slack bot is @mentioned in an existing thread for the first time, fetch prior messages via Slack's `conversations.replies` API and inject them as `input.message` events into the new session. The agent now sees the full thread history.

## Why
Previously, mentioning the bot mid-thread created a new session with zero context — the agent had no idea what the conversation was about.

## How
- On new session creation (PerThread strategy, `thread_ts` present), call `conversations.replies` to fetch up to 100 prior messages
- Inject each message as `input.message` event via `EventService::emit` (no workflow trigger)
- Bot messages → assistant role; human messages → user role with `ExternalActor` attribution
- All failures are non-fatal — agent proceeds without history
- Required scopes already in the generated manifest

## Risk
- Low
- Non-fatal error handling means existing functionality is unaffected

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added or updated (67 slack_events tests, 5 new)
- [x] Backward compatibility considered
- [x] Spec updated (`specs/slack-integration.md`)

body:
## Summary
This PR implements automatic synchronization of global cell selection (from ContextBar) to the Structure tab's editing selection, improving the user experience by allowing users to click cells in ContextBar and have them automatically selected for editing in the Structure tab.

## Key Changes
- Added `useEffect` hook to detect external `selectedCell` changes and map them to the correct `structureSelection` state
- Introduced `lastInternalCell` ref to distinguish between internal (Structure tab) selections and external (ContextBar) selections
- Updated `onSelectCell` handler to track internal selections via the ref, preventing the useEffect from overriding user-initiated deselections
- Updated comments to reflect the new approach: ring indicator now serves as a secondary indicator when selections differ, with primary sync handled by the useEffect

## Implementation Details
- The useEffect performs reverse-mapping of the global `cellIndex` to the correct section and sub-index within the normalized structure
- For single-subdivision sections, selection is mapped to the section level; for subdivided sections, it maps to the specific cell
- The ref guard ensures that toggling selections within the Structure tab (which sets `structureSelection` to null) isn't immediately overridden by the sync logic
- Handles edge cases like fullbleed layouts and empty structures by normalizing to a default single-section structure

body:
This PR introduces v5.5.0 — Spectral–Boundary Alignment Diagnostics, a new deterministic diagnostic layer for analyzing the relationship between Tanner graph spectral structure and belief propagation (BP) decision boundaries.

The diagnostic measures the cosine alignment between localized spectral eigenvectors of the Tanner graph and BP decision boundary directions, enabling investigation of whether structural spectral modes correspond to fragile decoding directions.

This continues the v5 research series exploring the geometry of BP decoding:

Tanner graph structure
↓
spectral localization
↓
decision boundary geometry
↓
attractor escape barriers
↓
decoder failure behavior

The feature integrates with the existing deterministic benchmark harness and records alignment metrics alongside boundary and barrier diagnostics.

Added
Spectral–Boundary Alignment Diagnostic

New module:

src/qec/diagnostics/spectral_boundary_alignment.py

Function:

compute_spectral_boundary_alignment(
    spectral_modes,
    boundary_direction
)

Computes cosine similarity between Tanner spectral modes and BP decision boundary directions:

alignment = |v · d| / (||v|| ||d||)

Output metrics:

alignment_scores
max_alignment
mean_alignment
dominant_alignment_mode
mode_count

The diagnostic is:

deterministic

observational

JSON-serializable

independent of decoder logic

No modifications were made to the BP decoder core.

Benchmark Harness Integration

bench/dps_v381_eval.py

New CLI flag:

--spectral-boundary-alignment

Automatically enables required diagnostics:

--tanner-spectral-analysis
--bp-boundary-analysis
--bp-barrier-analysis

The harness extracts:

localized Tanner spectral modes

BP decision boundary direction

and computes alignment metrics using the v5.5 diagnostic.

Experiment outputs now include:

alignment_max
alignment_mean
dominant_alignment_mode
mode_count
boundary_eps
barrier_eps
FER
Research Documentation

New report:

docs/reports/v5.5_spectral_boundary_alignment.md

The report describes:

theoretical motivation

deterministic algorithm design

integration with existing diagnostics

experimental methodology for evaluating correlations with FER.

Tests

New test suite:

tests/test_spectral_boundary_alignment.py

Coverage includes:

cosine similarity correctness

orthogonal / parallel vector cases

deterministic repeated execution

zero-vector handling

dominant mode detection

JSON serialization stability

input validation

All tests pass.

Design Principles

This feature follows the core architectural rules of the QEC framework:

deterministic execution

observational diagnostics only

no modification of decoder internals

JSON-stable experiment outputs

The diagnostic functions purely as a research instrument for analyzing decoder geometry.

Research Goal

The alignment metric allows investigation of the hypothesis:

localized Tanner spectral modes
≈
fragile BP decision boundary directions

If strong correlations are observed between alignment and FER, spectral analysis may provide structural predictors of decoder fragility.

Summary

This PR completes the v5.5 diagnostic layer, extending the v5 decoding analysis stack:

v5.1  BP attractor barrier analysis
v5.3  BP decision boundary estimation
v5.4  Tanner spectral diagnostics
v5.5  spectral–boundary alignment

Together these diagnostics form a deterministic framework for studying the geometry of belief propagation decoding in QLDPC codes.

author: jnberkman
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: mobydickdick
body:
### Motivation
- The radius bracketing routinely favored shrinking for AC0812 variants because the source error mask was anchored to the current (too-small) radius, hiding mismatch pixels for growth candidates.
- This caused the optimizer to get stuck in a local minimum for simple cases (circle + horizontal arm) instead of expanding the circle to match the original raster.

### Description
- Change `_element_error_for_circle_radius` to build a conservative `source_mask_params` whose `r` is `max(current_r, probe_r)` so growth probes evaluate against an expanded source mask (`src/image_composite_converter.py`).
- Re-anchor arm/stem geometry on the expanded source-mask probe so connector geometry remains consistent when the source mask is enlarged.
- Add a regression test `test_element_error_for_circle_radius_uses_expanded_source_mask_for_growth` that asserts growth probes call `extract_badge_element_mask` with a radius at least as large as the probe radius (`tests/test_image_composite_converter.py`).

### Testing
- Ran the focused pytest selection: `pytest -q tests/test_image_composite_converter.py -k "ac0812 or circle_radius_uses_expanded_source_mask_for_growth"` which reported `4 passed, 3 skipped, 63 deselected`.
- The new unit test verifies the exported behavior by monkeypatching rendering/error helpers and observing the mask radius used during evaluation.

author: haohlin
body:
## New Features

### Train/Validation Split
`--val_ratio 0.1` splits data for proper evaluation. Validation loss reported per epoch per layer. Set to 0 to disable.

### Early Stopping
`--patience 5` stops training a layer if validation loss doesn't improve for N epochs. Restores best weights automatically. `--min_delta` controls minimum improvement threshold.

### Learning Rate Warmup
`--warmup_epochs 3` linearly ramps LR from 0 to target over N epochs before applying step decay.

### Configurable Noise Types
`--noise_type` now supports:
- `salt_and_pepper` (default) — random min/max corruption
- `gaussian` — additive Gaussian noise scaled by data range
- `masking` — random zero-out

All noise functions extracted to `noise.py` with clean registry pattern.

### TensorBoard Logging
`--tensorboard` enables loss and LR logging per layer. View with `tensorboard --logdir runs/`.

### Final Evaluation
After all layers trained, reports reconstruction loss on validation set (or train set if no val split).

## Code Quality
- Training logic removed from `model.py` — models are now pure architecture
- Proper `logging` module instead of `print()`
- `torch.no_grad()` in inference paths
- `weights_only` param for `torch.load`
- 31 passing tests (model + noise + utils)

## Example
```bash
python train.py --noise_type gaussian --val_ratio 0.1 --patience 5 --warmup_epochs 3 --tensorboard
```

body:
Adds `user_feedback.py` — an in-memory system for collecting and querying user feedback with input validation.

## New module: `user_feedback.py`

- **`FeedbackStore.submit(name, email, rating, comment="")`** — validates inputs, stores feedback, returns a `Feedback` instance with auto-incremented ID and UTC timestamp
- **`FeedbackStore.get(id)`** / **`.all()`** / **`.filter_by_rating(rating)`** / **`.average_rating()`** — retrieval and aggregation
- **`Feedback.to_dict()`** — plain-dict serialization
- **`ValidationError`** / **`FeedbackNotFoundError`** — typed exceptions

| Field | Constraints |
|---|---|
| `name` | 1–100 chars (stripped) |
| `email` | must match `<local>@<domain>.<tld>` |
| `rating` | `int` 1–5; booleans and floats rejected |
| `comment` | `str`, max 1000 chars, optional |

```python
store = FeedbackStore()
fb = store.submit("Alice", "alice@example.com", 5, "Love it!")
store.average_rating()  # 5.0
store.filter_by_rating(5)  # [fb]
fb.to_dict()  # {"feedback_id": 1, "name": "Alice", ...}
```

## Tests: `test_user_feedback.py`

42 tests covering happy path, all validation branches, `filter_by_rating`, `average_rating`, `get`, and `to_dict`.

author: alokr-dhub
body:
# Summary

Glue jobs that read from or write to JDBC sources (Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, Redshift, Oracle, SQL Server) now produce lineage edges in DataHub. Previously these nodes fell through to the "unsupported connector" path and were silently skipped.
Added JDBC_PLATFORM_MAP to map JDBC protocol names to DataHub platform names, and JDBC_DEFAULT_SCHEMA to inject the correct default schema (public for Postgres/Redshift, dbo for SQL Server) when dbtable has no schema prefix.
The dataset URN is constructed as database.schema.table to match what the native source connectors (e.g. postgres, mysql) produce, enabling lineage stitching without additional configuration.
No new dataset MCEs are emitted for JDBC nodes — the datasets are expected to already exist from a separate source connector ingestion run.

author: nicoacosta
body:
## Summary
- **Problem:** The `ProcessScanner._is_claude_process()` method matches any process whose basename is `claude`, which incorrectly includes the Claude Desktop app (`/Applications/Claude.app/Contents/MacOS/Claude`) and all its Electron helper subprocesses (GPU, renderer, network, plugin). This creates ~8-10 ghost "Process detected — no hooks" sessions with 0% CPU and multi-hour uptimes.
- **Fix:** Added `_EXCLUDED_PATHS = ("claude.app",)` to `ProcessScanner`, filtering out any process whose command path contains `claude.app` (case-insensitive). This excludes the main Desktop binary and all helpers while still matching the CLI `claude` binary at paths like `~/.claude/local/claude`.
- **No false positives:** The CLI binary never has `claude.app` in its path, so legitimate sessions are unaffected.

## Changes
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/monitorator/scanner.py` | Added `_EXCLUDED_PATHS` tuple and path-fragment exclusion loop in `_is_claude_process()` |
| `tests/test_scanner.py` | Added `test_excludes_claude_desktop_app` covering main process, GPU helper, and renderer helper |

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/test_scanner.py` — all 25 tests pass
- [ ] `uv run monitorator` — verify ghost sessions no longer appear when Claude Desktop is running
- [ ] Verify real `claude` CLI sessions still appear normally

author: lammesen
body:
### Motivation
- Implement the core Symphony service described in SPEC.md: load repository-owned `WORKFLOW.md`, maintain per-issue workspaces, poll an issue tracker, and run coding-agent sessions in a reliable orchestrator loop.
- Focus on a stable, conformance-oriented Rust implementation of the essential layers (workflow loader, typed config, tracker adapter, workspace manager, agent runner, and orchestrator) rather than optional extensions.

### Description
- Bootstrapped a Rust binary/library crate and added async, HTTP, templating, and structured-logging dependencies in `Cargo.toml`.
- Implemented `WORKFLOW.md` loader in `src/workflow.rs` that strictly parses YAML front matter and the prompt body, validates presence, and supports reload-on-change via `reload_if_changed`.
- Added a typed config layer in `src/config.rs` that decodes front matter into runtime structs, applies defaults, expands `$ENV` indirection and normalizes workspace paths and hook/agent defaults (hook timeout `60000ms`, codex command default `codex app-server`, retry backoff cap `300000ms`, etc.).
- Implemented a normalized `Issue` model and a Linear GraphQL client in `src/tracker.rs` that supports candidate fetch, state refresh by IDs, and terminal-issue fetch.
- Implemented per-issue workspace management in `src/workspace.rs` with sanitized workspace keys, directory creation, lifecycle hooks (`after_create`, `before_run`, `after_run`, `before_remove`), hook timeout enforcement, and cleanup.
- Implemented an agent runner in `src/agent.rs` that uses Handlebars in strict mode to render prompts (only `issue` + `attempt`), launches the configured codex app-server command, writes a JSON-RPC-like session start, parses JSON-lines from stdout (handles stderr separately), and enforces request/turn timeouts.
- Implemented the orchestrator loop in `src/orchestrator.rs` which performs startup terminal-workspace cleanup, periodic ticks with dynamic workflow reload, reconciliation of running issues, bounded-concurrency dispatch via a semaphore, and an exponential backoff retry queue for failed/continuation runs; logs structured session fields (`issue_id`, `issue_identifier`, `session_id`).
- Implemented CLI entrypoint `src/main.rs` that accepts an optional positional `WORKFLOW.md` path (defaults to `./WORKFLOW.md`) and initializes JSON structured logging.

### Testing
- Ran formatter and unit tests via `cargo fmt && cargo test`; both completed successfully.
- `cargo test` executed the included unit test for front-matter parsing (`workflow::tests::parses_front_matter`) which passed.
- The repository builds and library tests finished without failures in the test profile (`cargo test` finished OK).

author: osalotioman
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive automation system for issue and pull request management using GitHub Actions and templates. The main focus is to streamline claiming, disclaiming, proposing, withdrawing, and reviewing issues and PRs, as well as to improve documentation and workflow clarity. The changes enable contributors to interact with issues and PRs using specific comment commands, which trigger automated workflows for assignment, status updates, and project board transitions.

Issue and PR workflow automation:

* Added `.github/workflows/01-claim-issue.yml` to automate issue claiming via "claim" comments, assigning users and updating project board status.
* Added `.github/workflows/02-disclaim-issue.yml` to automate disclaiming issues via "disclaim" comments, removing assignees and reverting project status.
* Added `.github/workflows/03-propose-pr.yml` to automate linking PRs to issues and moving issues to "In Progress" when a "propose" comment is made.
* Added `.github/workflows/04-withdraw-pr.yml` to automate unlinking PRs from issues and moving issues back to "Claimed" when a "withdraw" comment is made.
* Added `.github/workflows/05-pr-comment.yml` to automate labeling PRs as "awaiting-author" or "awaiting-review" and updating project board status based on comment triggers.

Issue template and documentation improvements:

* Added `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` to enable blank issues and provide a link to the contributing guide for clarity on expectations.
* Added `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/task.yml` to introduce a structured template for maintenance, refactoring, and documentation tasks, including area selection and confirmation checklist.
